name: Medpill

card.summary: Looksmaxxing slang for the belief that Mediterranean and dark-featured looks are strongly preferred, used by members to reassess which features count as attractive.
card.note: A community term; threads using it often involve ethnic generalisations that are contested.

quick.overview:
Medpill is a term from looksmaxxing forums, formed on the model of blackpill and redpill. In the threads where it appears it refers to the claim that Mediterranean or dark-featured men, with darker hair, eyes and skin tones, are attractive to women and outperform fairer Nordic-type features.

Members use it to point to anecdotes, such as a woman praising a tanned, dark-haired partner, and to argue that colouring matters in how people are perceived. It is a community claim rather than a researched concept.
quick.how: In practice it appears as forum threads sharing anecdotes and photographs. Members who accept the idea may talk about tanning, hair colour and darker-toned styling, though the term mostly functions as a discussion label.
quick.risks: The label is discussed in threads that mix appearance talk with ethnic generalisations, and attractiveness research reports that preferences vary by person and culture. It carries no direct physical risks; tanning has well-documented skin-cancer risk.

lead: Medpill is slang used on looksmax.org and related forums. In the threads where it is used, it denotes the belief that Mediterranean and dark-featured men are preferred by women over fairer, Nordic-type men [1].

The format follows other pill terms: a thread presents a story or anecdote, such as a woman describing her partner's tanned skin, green eyes and dark hair, as the revelation, and members discuss whether colouring helps attractiveness [1]. Participants usually treat it as part of broader debate on how ethnicity and colouring affect perception.

chain: Adopt the belief that dark features are preferred
Adjust colouring and styling, such as tan and darker tones
Aim for a look members regard as more attractive
angle.text: Believers use the idea to reassess which of their features help them and to experiment with colouring and styling. It is a perspective rather than a procedure.

infobox: Looksmaxxing forums, modelled on redpill and blackpill

paras: The term appears in forum thread titles that frame a story as a revelation, with members adding their own anecdotes and photos in replies [1].

Proponents say anecdotes, such as a woman bragging about a tanned, dark-haired partner, show that fair colouring is not the only preferred look [1]. Critics within the forums and outside them point out that such cases are individual and that preferences vary.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the term appears in thread titles presenting anecdotes about colouring and attraction [1].

claims.claim: Mediterranean or dark colouring is preferred over fair Nordic colouring
claims.believers: Members share anecdotes, such as a woman praising a tanned, green-eyed, dark-haired boyfriend, as evidence [1].
claims.experts: No published study has tested the term as defined in these forums; attractiveness research generally reports preferences that vary by individual and culture.
